A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the XXL Survey superclusters, and in particular XLSSsC01, are not yet in a mature state of evolution, and their galaxy populations are still in the process of being assembled.
the environment in this supercluster has a strong effect on the colour and morphology, and a mild effect on the star-formation activity of galaxies.

The main takeaway from our work is that
environment has little impact on the star formation properties of the galaxies in the supercluster, but it does play a role in the quenching process of the most massive galaxies.

the stellar populations of massive galaxies in clusters are already quenched at high redshift, and that the quenching of star formation in massive galaxies is a process that takes place in a relatively short timescale, of order 0.5-1 Gyr, and that is completed at high redshift.
the environment is more effective in quenching the star formation activity of galaxies in the low-mass end, and that the quenching of massive galaxies is likely driven by internal processes.
